# CNA C API Coverage Matrix

<!-- Generated by tools/c-api/generate_coverage_inventory.py; do not edit by hand. -->

## Coverage contract

This file is the complete reviewed CBIND-033 inventory of CNA's public C++ declaration
surface. It is generated from every `modules/*/include/Microsoft/**/*.hpp` and
`modules/*/include/CNA/**/*.hpp` header. Paths containing the explicit implementation
segments `Internal` or `Detail`, the whole `modules/platform` module, and the C API's own
`.h` headers, are excluded. The platform module is excluded as a **substrate**: the C ABI is
built on it and a C caller reaches platform behaviour through the routes that use it, never
through `IPlatform` -- an owner decision of 2026-08-16, recorded as `CBIND-047`. A
header remains listed even when it declares no public/protected symbol.

Every symbol below has a stable content-derived `CPP-*` ID, a C-native mapping, required
test evidence and a status. `implemented` means an explicit rule names existing C API
and tests; `partial` means the named C route covers only the stated specialization or
subset; `planned` is not coverage and names the task that owns its design; and
`not-applicable` records an explicitly deleted operation that has no callable source
behavior to expose. Nothing is treated as implemented merely because a related C
operation exists.

Snapshot: **420 headers**, **6694 symbols**, **6296 implemented**, **12 partial**, **0 planned**, **386 not applicable**. Explicitly excluded internal/detail headers: **120**.

Regenerate with:

```bash
python3 tools/c-api/generate_coverage_inventory.py --write
python3 tools/c-api/generate_coverage_inventory.py --check
```

`--check` is a mandatory gate (CBIND-043), enforced in two places: the CTest test
`CApiCoverageMatrix`, registered under `CNA_BUILD_TESTS`, and the build-free
`.github/workflows/c-api-coverage-gate.yml` workflow, which runs on every push.

## Status definitions

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ✅ implemented | Exact current C mapping and C-only evidence are named. |
| 🟨 partial | A useful specialization/subset exists, but the source symbol is not fully mapped. |
| ⬜ planned | No complete C mapping exists; the owner task and required evidence are explicit. |
| ➖ not applicable | The public declaration explicitly deletes this operation, so no callable C++ behavior exists to map. |

| `CPP-628DE46DBF9C` | 22 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Audio::DynamicSoundEffectInstance` | an owned handle of the **same kind** as an ordinary sound-effect instance, created by `cna_dynamic_sound_effect_instance_create` from a sample rate and channel count rather than from a sound effect. Every `cna_sound_effect_instance_*` route therefore accepts it — the transport, the mixing setters, the state query and the destroy — and the canonical overrides dispatch virtually behind them. What this kind adds is the buffer queue: the pending count, the byte and float submit routes, the initial-buffer and clear routes, the queue advance and the buffer-needed subscription, plus the two **instance-level** sample computations that use the rate and channels the instance was created with. **Submitted bytes are copied**, which is what makes the route safe to call from a producer thread while playback runs. A streaming instance has **no parent sound effect**, so the instance-count bookkeeping a sound-effect child carries has nothing to point at; a route that needs streaming refuses an ordinary instance with `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_STATE` | `AudioStreamingSmoke.c` creates one, drives it through the ordinary instance routes to prove the shared kind, checks both instance-level computations against a known tenth of a second, submits bytes and asserts the pending count rises and survives the caller overwriting its own buffer, submits floats, refuses three bad ranges, subscribes to and detaches the buffer-needed event, clears the queue back to empty, and asserts an ordinary instance refuses every streaming route | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037F2`) |

| `CPP-C68C594B0752` | 43 | public class | `Microsoft::Devices::VibrateController` | free routes rather than a handle, because the canonical controller is a **process-wide singleton** that is never constructed or destroyed by a caller: `cna_vibrate_controller_start`, `_start_with_intensity_ext`, `_start_left_right_ext`, `_stop`, `_get_is_supported_ext` and the device-name count/copy pair, each taking the game handle for thread affinity. The canonical asymmetry is preserved rather than tidied: the **duration is bounded** on all three start routes and a value outside zero to five seconds is refused, while the **intensity is clamped**, with a not-a-number strength becoming no vibration rather than reaching the platform undefined. `cna_vibrate_controller_set_test_backend_ext` supplies this ABI's own backend where the canonical hook takes a C++ object, and `_get_test_log_ext` reads back what it was asked to do | `DevicesSmoke.c` installs the test backend and proves each request arrives with its own arguments: the implied full intensity of the single-argument start, the clamped over-range intensity, the not-a-number strength becoming zero, both motor strengths carried separately, the stop, and the refused six-second and negative durations on both start families. A frame lands in a `Texture2D` **the caller owns and keeps**, which is the canonical contract and deliberately not the borrowed per-frame texture `CBIND-037C7` settled for video — nothing here is invalidated by the next call. Two canonical behaviors are preserved rather than corrected: having no frame ready is an ordinary `CNA_FALSE` rather than a failure, and **a texture whose size does not match the frame is refused the same way**, with no resize and no distinct reason. | `CPP-89E657CBD458` | 25 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::GamerServices::AvatarDescription` | an owned handle with one info snapshot, a byte copy, both random factories and a gamer read that folds the canonical begin/end pair into one route that then invokes the callback -- the canonical read completes before its own begin returns. A description is **exactly `CNA_AVATAR_DESCRIPTION_BYTE_COUNT` bytes** and any other length is refused, which is what the canonical constructor does; whether it is *valid* is a separate question its first byte answers. **Two fields are constant on this runtime**: the height is always zero and the body type always female, because the canonical format carries neither and the implementation says so rather than guessing -- asking for a male body still reports female. The change notification is a **static** event, so its subscription takes no description | `AvatarsSmoke.c` builds a random description and asserts its exact size, its constant height and body type, copies its bytes and refuses a too-small buffer, asserts a wrong-length description is refused while a correct one is accepted and its validity follows its first byte, reads a gamer's description and asserts the callback ran once, and subscribes to and releases the change notification | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037G7`) |

| `CPP-36BF8DE71F67` | 15 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::GamerServices::GamerPrivilegeException` | boundary conversions rather than types, following the audio exceptions exactly: the firewall in `CnaCApiDetail.hpp` catches all six and answers four different results, because the differences are what a caller acts on. No gamer services at all and a title that needs updating are both `CNA_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED` — nothing the caller supplies or retries changes either. An absent network and a privilege the gamer does not have are both `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_STATE`, the shape a disconnected storage device already has, as is a guide that is already visible. A network operation that failed while the network was available is `CNA_RESULT_PLATFORM`: a native service failed and a retry may get past it. The constructors are the canonical ways to raise one, which C never does — it only receives them. **The arm order matters**: the net module's `NetworkSessionJoinException` derives from this module's `NetworkException`, so the two modules share one hierarchy and the derived arms sit before their base | `BoundaryDetailTest.cpp` throws each of the six through the firewall and asserts the result, the category and the canonical message, including that an absent network is distinguishable from a network operation that failed while connected — which is exactly what a mis-ordered arm would break | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037G3`) |

An absent network and a privilege the gamer does not have are both `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_STATE`, the shape a disconnected storage device already has, as is a guide that is already visible. A network operation that failed while the network was available is `CNA_RESULT_PLATFORM`: a native service failed and a retry may get past it. The constructors are the canonical ways to raise one, which C never does — it only receives them. **The arm order matters**: the net module's `NetworkSessionJoinException` derives from this module's `NetworkException`, so the two modules share one hierarchy and the derived arms sit before their base | `BoundaryDetailTest.cpp` throws each of the six through the firewall and asserts the result, the category and the canonical message, including that an absent network is distinguishable from a network operation that failed while connected — which is exactly what a mis-ordered arm would break | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037G3`) |

| `CPP-DE30D454DC4E` | 15 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::GamerServices::GuideAlreadyVisibleException` | boundary conversions rather than types, following the audio exceptions exactly: the firewall in `CnaCApiDetail.hpp` catches all six and answers four different results, because the differences are what a caller acts on. No gamer services at all and a title that needs updating are both `CNA_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED` — nothing the caller supplies or retries changes either. An absent network and a privilege the gamer does not have are both `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_STATE`, the shape a disconnected storage device already has, as is a guide that is already visible. A network operation that failed while the network was available is `CNA_RESULT_PLATFORM`: a native service failed and a retry may get past it. The constructors are the canonical ways to raise one, which C never does — it only receives them. **The arm order matters**: the net module's `NetworkSessionJoinException` derives from this module's `NetworkException`, so the two modules share one hierarchy and the derived arms sit before their base | `BoundaryDetailTest.cpp` throws each of the six through the firewall and asserts the result, the category and the canonical message, including that an absent network is distinguishable from a network operation that failed while connected — which is exactly what a mis-ordered arm would break | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037G3`) |

| `CPP-8C6F6F3704F7` | 14 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::GamerServices::LeaderboardEntry` | an owned handle with one info snapshot, a rating setter, a gamer query, a columns handle and `cna_leaderboard_entry_equals` behind both canonical operators -- entries compare by **gamer, rating and ranking**, not by their columns. The columns handle **aliases the entry's own dictionary**, so writing through it changes the entry, and it keeps the entry alive for as long as it names them. | `CPP-F30FE2CA729B` | 11 | public struct | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::GamerServices::LeaderboardIdentity` | the fixed value `CNA_LeaderboardIdentity`, with `cna_leaderboard_identity_init` mapping both canonical creation routes -- the one without a game mode is this one with zero. The key is carried **inline** rather than as a pointer, so an identity is a value a caller can build on the stack and pass by address; the canonical keys are short names, and a key that does not fit the inline capacity is **refused rather than truncated**, as is one with no terminator inside it. #### `modules/gamer-services/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/GamerServices/LeaderboardWriter.hpp`

| ID | Line | Access/kind | C++ symbol | C mapping | Tests | Status |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CPP-5921A31E966B` | 16 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::GamerServices::LeaderboardWriter` | no C form, and the reason is a constraint the canonical source states outright: a `LeaderboardWriter` **captures its owning gamer's address at construction and neither it nor `Gamer` re-points that pointer on a copy**, so a gamer's address must never change once its writer may be used. Every gamer this ABI publishes is a copy of the value the canonical factory returns, so its writer's owner already dangles -- reaching it crashes rather than writing a score. Binding it would hand a C caller a route that cannot be used safely. The entries a **reader** hands out are still fully mapped; they are snapshots, and nothing in this ABI writes a score back | not applicable; the route is deliberately absent rather than present and unsafe | ➖ not applicable (`CBIND-037G6c`) |

#### `modules/gamer-services/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/GamerServices/NetworkException.hpp`

| `CPP-336B5B958FC5` | 15 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::GamerServices::NetworkException` | boundary conversions rather than types, following the audio exceptions exactly: the firewall in `CnaCApiDetail.hpp` catches all six and answers four different results, because the differences are what a caller acts on. No gamer services at all and a title that needs updating are both `CNA_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED` — nothing the caller supplies or retries changes either. An absent network and a privilege the gamer does not have are both `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_STATE`, the shape a disconnected storage device already has, as is a guide that is already visible. A network operation that failed while the network was available is `CNA_RESULT_PLATFORM`: a native service failed and a retry may get past it. The constructors are the canonical ways to raise one, which C never does — it only receives them. **The arm order matters**: the net module's `NetworkSessionJoinException` derives from this module's `NetworkException`, so the two modules share one hierarchy and the derived arms sit before their base | `BoundaryDetailTest.cpp` throws each of the six through the firewall and asserts the result, the category and the canonical message, including that an absent network is distinguishable from a network operation that failed while connected — which is exactly what a mis-ordered arm would break | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037G3`) |

| `CPP-E06AA0C98BAA` | 19 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::GamerServices::PropertyDictionary` | an owned handle with a **typed** route family. The nine canonical getters and eight setters map one-for-one, and `TryGetValue` becomes `cna_property_dictionary_try_get_value_kind_ext`, which answers **what kind of value a slot holds** -- that is what replaces reading the boxed value, since a C caller reading something it did not write has to know which getter to use. Every typed getter checks the kind **at the boundary** and refuses a mismatch with `INVALID_STATE`, rather than letting the canonical unboxing fail into a generic internal error nobody could act on; an unknown key is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, a different answer. The keys are walked by index, because the canonical key list and bulk copy both answer containers C cannot receive. The canonical destructor becomes `cna_haptic_device_destroy` and `Dispose` its own idempotent route, so a caller can close the device without giving up the handle — the same split `MouseCursor` uses. A closed device is not an error state: every route on it succeeds and answers `CNA_FALSE`, zero or -1 through its output, which is what makes the family usable with no force-feedback hardware. | `CPP-2C3442E7D8E2` | 33 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Input::GamePad` | one `cna_gamepad_*` route per canonical static, each taking an active game handle for the same reason the state and capability captures do — CNA is event-driven, so a device query is only meaningful on the game thread of a running game. `ExcludeAxisDeadZone` is the exception: it is a pure value operation and takes no handle. The class itself has no handle, because its canonical constructor is deleted and every member is static. Two canonical shapes are preserved rather than collapsed: a query that reports availability through its return value and its answer through an output reference keeps both answers separate in C — `_get_gyro_ext`, `_get_accelerometer_ext` and `_get_touchpad_finger_ext` each take an availability output, so "no sensor" is an ordinary answer, not a failure — and the four identity strings use the project count/copy protocol. The touchpad finger query returns its four output references as one fixed `CNA_GamePadTouchpadFinger` value. No `std::string`, `Vector3` or CNA::Input enumeration crosses the boundary | `InputSnapshotsSmoke.c` calls every route inside the update callback and asserts the shape of an empty slot answer for each — false, zero, empty or an `Unknown` identity — plus the count/copy round trip for all four identity strings, an out-of-range player slot and a null output refused per route, an undefined button bit refused by the label query, and the wrong-thread refusal; the pure dead-zone exclusion is covered outside the callback including its non-finite refusal leaving the output untouched. C and C++ ABI assertions freeze the three identity enumerations and the touchpad-finger layout. Runs under HEADLESS, SDL_RENDERER and SOFTWARE | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037B3`) |

| `CPP-C8523576EFDC` | 19 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Media::AlbumCollection` | one borrowed collection handle per element type — `CNA_AlbumCollectionHandle`, `CNA_ArtistCollectionHandle`, `CNA_GenreCollectionHandle`, `CNA_PlaylistCollectionHandle` — each with `_get_count`, `_get_at`, `_get_is_disposed`, `_dispose`, `_destroy` and a type-name count/copy pair. All four canonical types are structurally identical, so they share one C shape rather than four; `_get_at` returns a borrowed element handle that keeps the owning library alive, and the index is validated in C before the canonical indexer would throw. | `CPP-187387966869` | 22 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Media::MediaPlayer` | free `cna_media_player_*` routes, because C has no static class. Every route takes an active game handle for the same reason the input captures do — the player is process-wide state a running game owns. The three `Play` overloads become `_play_song`, `_play_songs` and `_play_songs_from`; **the canonical player copies the song it is given into its queue rather than taking it**, so a caller's handle is unaffected. Two canonical behaviors are preserved rather than tightened: the volume setter **clamps** to 0 through 1 instead of refusing, and the indexed `Play` overload does not range-check its index. The two static `EventHandler` events become owned registrations with one shared `cna_media_player_unsubscribe_ext`, and the canonical deferred raises are exposed as `_raise_active_song_changed_ext`/`_raise_media_state_changed_ext` so a C application can observe its own wiring. `Update`, `ProgramExit` and the elapsed-time song-end detector keep `_ext` suffixes, being CNA extensions; the detector's canonical rule is preserved exactly — a song whose duration is unknown never reports ended | `MediaPlayerSmoke.c` round-trips every flag and restores it, since these are process-wide settings the suite does not own; proves the volume clamp at both ends; drives the queue through `play`, `pause`, `resume` and `stop` asserting the transitions **as a relationship** — whether playback actually starts depends on the platform's ability to decode the file, not on the C API, so the suite asserts the paused/playing round trip only when playback began and the no-op contract otherwise; covers both event registrations end to end with per-registration detach; and proves the song-end detector reports nothing for an unknown duration and reports ended once a known one is exceeded | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037C6`) |

| `CPP-43541AECFE4D` | 16 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Media::MediaQueue` | a borrowed `CNA_MediaQueueHandle` from `cna_media_player_get_queue` — a view of the one process-lifetime queue, like a stock mouse cursor — with count, active index get/set, `_get_at`, `_get_active_song`, `_add`, `_clear` and a type-name pair. **Two deliberate deviations, both forced by ownership.** A queue entry crosses as an *independently owned copy* rather than a borrowed view, because the canonical queue destroys its entries whenever it is cleared — which every play route does — so a borrowed handle would dangle; the copy carries the same file and name and therefore compares equal to the entry. And `cna_media_queue_add` appends a *copy* too, because the canonical `Add` adopts the pointer it is given and C cannot hand a handle's object away without leaving the caller a stale handle — appending a copy is exactly what the canonical player itself does when it enqueues a song. The type name is addressed by index rather than being a free function, because the canonical member is an instance method and the source object is not constructible from outside the library | `MediaSmoke.c` enumerates every source the device reports, asserts at least one local-device source exists with a non-empty name, round-trips both strings with their exact byte counts, checks the fully-qualified type name literally, and covers the out-of-range index, null-output and buffer-too-small refusals on every route. The whole suite runs under ASan with leak detection on, which is what proves the borrowed-list release rather than a comment claiming it | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037C1`) |

| `CPP-52B29F038FD8` | 19 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Media::Picture` | a borrowed `CNA_PictureHandle` with the name count/copy pair, width, height, the containing album as an optional child, `cna_picture_equals` (canonically the resolved file path, which is also the token) and the hash. The canonical date is a `std::chrono` time point, so **the ABI gains its first point-in-time representation**: `cna_picture_get_date_unix_ticks` reports 100-nanosecond ticks counted from the Unix epoch — the same tick the duration routes use, but from a fixed epoch rather than from a duration's zero. | `CPP-CD3DC478E906` | 22 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Media::Video` | an owned `CNA_VideoHandle` from three routes: `cna_video_create` (the probing constructor), `cna_video_create_with_metadata` (the compiled-asset one, which never touches the file) and `cna_video_create_from_uri_ext`. Each takes a callback-scoped borrowed graphics-device handle, which is where the canonical device argument comes from. **The graphics device is reported as presence, not handed back**: a borrowed device handle is valid only inside the callback that produced it, so returning one from a video created in an earlier frame would be a promise this ABI cannot keep — `cna_video_get_has_graphics_device` answers the question the canonical null check asks. Two canonical behaviors are reported rather than corrected: a file that exists but cannot be decoded leaves width, height, frame rate and duration at **zero** instead of failing, and the URI factory **does not parse URIs** — it forwards the text straight to the file constructor, so a scheme-bearing string is simply a path that does not exist | `VideoSmoke.c` proves the missing-file refusal, the zeroed metadata of an existing but undecodable file, the exact declared metadata of the compiled-asset constructor including its duration in ticks, the file name and type name round trips, the unvalidated duration setter and both track selectors, and that the URI factory accepts a plain path while a `http:` string fails as a missing file | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037C7`) |

| `CPP-202000FD20E2` | 41 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Media::VideoPlayer` | an owned `CNA_VideoPlayerHandle` with the loop, mute, volume, position, state and video properties, the four transport routes, both track selectors, and the canonical dispose-versus-release split. **The frame texture is the slice's one hard problem, and it is solved by lifetime rather than by copying**: the player owns and replaces its frame texture, so `cna_video_player_get_texture` hands back a borrowed `CNA_Texture2DHandle` that the C layer itself **invalidates on the next call to that player** — any later route, including another `get_texture`, releases it, so a stale frame handle fails with `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_HANDLE` instead of touching freed memory. Asking before playback is an ordinary `CNA_FALSE`, because the canonical implementation deliberately answers null there where the original API faults. Playing a file the platform cannot decode leaves the player stopped rather than failing, and disposal makes every playback route report the canonical disposed-object failure while the disposal query keeps answering. The C resource retains the video it was told to play, so releasing the caller's video handle can never leave the player pointing at a destroyed video | `VideoSmoke.c` covers creation, every property round trip, the no-frame answer before playback, playing an undecodable file leaving the player stopped, the played video reported back, transport calls in every state, releasing the caller's video handle while the player still holds it, and disposal turning every playback route into `INVALID_STATE` while the disposal query still answers | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037C7`) |

| `CPP-4648B593894B` | 48 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::GraphicsDeviceManager` | an owned `CNA_GraphicsDeviceManagerHandle` from `cna_graphics_device_manager_create`, the two default back-buffer constants as macros, every preference as a get/set pair, the borrowed managed device, `_apply_changes`, `_toggle_full_screen`, `_create_device`, `_begin_draw`, `_end_draw`, `_dispose`, a type-name pair, `cna_graphics_device_manager_subscribe` for the five data-free events and `_subscribe_preparing_device_settings` for the one that carries data. Creating the manager **registers both services**, which is what `cna_game_services_contains_ext` then reports, and a game accepts exactly one. Every reconfiguration reports `CNA_RESULT_PLATFORM` when the platform declines, the rule the window slice established. **Releasing a manager keeps the object alive until its game is destroyed**: the canonical game caches a raw pointer to the graphics device service and never clears it, so destroying the manager first would leave the game dereferencing freed memory on its next frame — a canonical defect this ABI works around rather than exposes | `GraphicsDeviceManagerSmoke.c` creates the manager and asserts both services appear, refuses a second manager, round-trips every preference and refuses every undefined identity, proves the orientation bit set accepts a combination, borrows the managed device, applies the changes and re-creates the device accepting a platform refusal as correct, runs the draw bracket, asserts disposal unregisters both services and raises its event exactly once across two disposals, and covers every released-handle refusal. The retained-object rule is proved by the suite running clean under ASan, where the earlier design reproduced a heap-use-after-free on the very next frame | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037E4`) |

| `CPP-49977617E59C` | 13 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::IDrawable` | not types in C, and the one place in this ABI where the caller **provides** behavior rather than consuming it: C cannot implement a C++ interface, so a component is a `CNA_GameComponentCallbacks` set plus a context, and this ABI supplies the object that implements all three interfaces and forwards to it. Each interface operation is one member of that set or one route — initialization, the per-frame update and draw, the enabled, update-order, draw-order and visibility queries, and the four change events reached through `cna_game_component_subscribe`. A null callback member is simply not called, which is how a C component opts out of a step | `RuntimeComponentsSmoke.c` builds one component of each kind, drives initialization, update and draw through the C routes and asserts each handler ran with the frame's own time, reads every interface query back, and covers the refusals a component that does not draw returns for every drawing route | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037E1`) |
